It aired on [[February 9]], [[2013]]. ==Official description== ''"''Anakin and Ahsoka investigate a deadly bombing at the Jedi Temple''."'' ==Opening narration== {{OpeningCrawl |name=Episode 17
SABOTAGE |text=Invasion! The planet Cato Neimoidia is under Separatist attack. Anakin Skywalker and his Padawan, Ahsoka Tano, rush to the rescue as they lead a squadron of starfighters to the planet below....}} ==Plot summary== {{Quote|People blamed Jedi because of you. People were killed because of you!|Ahsoka Tano, to Letta Turmond|}} [[Anakin Skywalker]] and [[Ahsoka Tano]] are sent to a [[Defense of Cato Neimoidia|battle]] on [[Cato Neimoidia]] by the [[Jedi High Council]] to rescue the world from an invasion set by the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatists]]. Anakin's [[Eta-2 Actis-class light interceptor|starfighter]] is attacked by [[Pistoeka sabotage droid|buzz droids]], who severely damage the ship. Anakin is knocked out by a powerful shock from his damaged starfighter leaving [[R2-D2]] in control of the ship. Ahsoka instructs R2-D2 to land the ship while she pulls Anakin out. Shortly after they are contacted by [[Yoda]], summoning them back to the [[Imperial Palace|Jedi Temple]] to investigate a bombing. It is rumored that a [[Jedi]] may have caused the blast, so Anakin and Ahsoka, having been off-world at the time, have been selected to lead the investigation. They are aided by the droid [[Russo-ISC]] in their investigation and together he and Tano go to interview the survivors of the blast. There they find a potential suspect, [[Jackar Bowmani]]. Anakin finds Bowmani's wife, [[Letta Turmond]], in a protest outside the Temple. She protests that her husband could not have had anything to do with the explosion. While analyzing the explosion, they discover the blast origin, a transport, and find that is is covered in explosive [[NM-K reconstitutor|Nano-droids]]. They also manage to find Jackar's hand, the only part of him that survived the explosion. Nano-droids are discovered in his [[blood]]stream, leading them to believe that he "was the bomb." Together, Anakin and Ahsoka go to his house to search for more nano-droids, finding them in the food. Suspecting that someone fed the droids to Jackar, they are interrupted by Letta. They decide to bring her back to the temple for more questioning, suspecting that she might know more than she is telling them. However, Letta makes a run for it and the two Jedi follow, chasing her through the streets. Finally they corner her in an alley. Both of the Jedi now believe that she was responsible for the explosion and faced with Anakin's anger she admits to it. The Jedi bring her back to the temple. Although still unaware of her motives, they intend to question her further. Back at the Jedi Temple, Russo informs Anakin and Ahsoka that his investigation confirms no Jedi were involved in the explosion. [[Mace Windu]] voices his opinion that the reason behind the bombing was meant to turn public sentiment against the Jedi and the Clone Wars. Anakin and Ahsoka discuss their own fears that a Jedi might have been the perpetrator; Anakin remarks that while there will be Jedi who disappoint, the greater number of Jedi fighting for the right thing will balance it out. ==Continuity== The episode was named for [[Wikipedia:Alfred Hitchcock|Alfred Hitchcock's]] 1936 film [[Wikipedia:Sabotage (film)|''Sabotage'']]. All four episodes of the story arc in fact were named after various Hitchcock narratives.{{SW|url=series/clone-wars/sabotage-trivia-gallery|text="Sabotage" Trivia Gallery}} Anakin Skywalker's statement to Ahsoka Tano, "I'm afraid one can eventually become the other," was in reference to past betrayals of the Jedi by political idealists, including [[Dooku|Count Dooku]] and Season 4's General [[Pong Krell]]. Russo-ISC's characterizations and name alluded to [[Wikipedia:David Caruso|David Caruso's]] role in the crime drama series ''[[Wikipedia:CSI: Miami|CSI Miami]]''. The gunship that delivers Captain Rex to Cato Neimoidia was the ''[[Lucky Lekku]]''. The rest of the troops on the gunship are [[clone jetpack trooper]]s, which makes it the first appearance of the clone jetpack trooper in [[canon]]. The guards seen at the temple during Anakin's interaction with Cin Drallig, named Temple Guards, were confirmed to be making more appearances throughout the arc. The signs among the temple protest groups included a clone trooper behind a cross out sign, and Aurebesh phrases that state "The Jedi are Corrupt" and "Stop Cloning Violence." Although it was destroyed during the episode, [[Anakin Skywalker's Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor|Anakin's Eta-2 interceptor]] appeared for the first time in the series. ==Media==
